messages:
Megan (AE): ACME wants clarity on key custody for sealed/offline installs: can Redwood sign bundles centrally or do they require a customer HSM? Also need the upgrade cadence spelled out for procurement.
Tomas (SE): We support both: Redwood-signed bundles and customer-managed signing via HSM. For HSM we provide a signing utility that talks to PKCS#11 endpoints during bundle creation (offline signing workflow).
Victor (ACME Ops): Important: our auditors demand key escrow or split-key custody for the pilot. Can Redwood facilitate an escrow workflow or do we need a third-party CA?
Karen (Security): We can support split-signature workflows. Options:
- Redwood signs primary artifact and customer cosigns with HSM (m-of-n signing)
- Customer provides a dedicated signing key stored in their HSM; Redwood produces unsigned bundles and a signing manifest.
We can also notarize with a timestamp authority.
Tomas (SE): Operational notes: installer looks for a chain of signatures in `manifest.json`. If multiple signatures present, installer verifies that at least one comes from an allowed fingerprint list. That supports cosign or m-of-n.
Megan (AE): Procurement follow-up: how do these options change pricing and SOW?
Lara (Legal): Pricing: Redwood-signed bundles are included in premium onprem support. HSM integration and bespoke escrow/legal work are billable PS items. We can include a one-time HSM integration engineering credit in the SOW for large deals.
Victor (ACME Ops): For the POC we want a push model via sneakernet but with a central jumpbox that can perform OCSP checks when temporarily networked. Is that supported?
Tomas (SE): Yes. We provide an optional jumpbox workflow: customer ingests USB into an airgapped jumpbox, runs `redwood-verify --stapled-ocsp ocsp-response.der` if online; otherwise it validates against the bundled OCSP stapled response. We recommend stapled OCSP in the notarized manifest for low-connectivity sites.
Karen (Security): Auditables: we'll provide per-bundle SBOM, cert fingerprints, OCSP stapled responses, and a tamper-evident manifest. Also include a test-harness with smoke tests for the customer's ops to run pre-apply.
Megan (AE): Upgrade cadence: what do we recommend for a conservative enterprise?
Tomas (SE): Recommendation: monthly security deltas (minimal token changes), quarterly functional bundles, and a hotfix track for critical CVEs. Hotfixes: included (2/year) with premium support, extra are PS. Rollback artifact always shipped as pre-signed archive.
Victor (ACME Ops): Sounds good. Last ask: can Redwood output a compliance-ready runbook we hand to our change board with exact commands and signatures to verify?
Karen (Security): Yes, we'll produce a runbook appendix with commands, example `manifest.json`, PKCS#11 integration notes, and a checklist for GRC.
publish-bot: Offline bundle created: `redwood-offline-escrow-2026-07-11.tar.gz` sha256=e5b1c8a2f3d4e6b7c8d9e0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f9a0b1 (sig=SIG_escrow_v1).
Megan (AE): I'll update the commercial slide + SOW draft (include one-time HSM integration PS line) and circulate to ACME. Victor, expect SOW comments in 3 business days?
Victor (ACME Ops): Yes, will coordinate with GRC and procurement. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
